Visualize Joint-RPCA results

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotJointRPCA.R
plotJointRPCA.Rd

These functions visualize Joint-RPCA results stored in a SingleCellExperiment or MultiAssayExperiment.

  • plotJointRPCA() creates a two-dimensional ordination plot of the samples.

  • plotJointRPCACovariance() creates a heatmap of the feature-feature covariance (or correlation), split into blocks by data layer.

  • plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance() creates a heatmap showing how the variance of each data layer, or of each feature, is divided across the components.

  • plotJointRPCANetwork() creates a network where nodes are features and edges connect features with strong covariance (or correlation).

  • plotJointRPCALoadings() shows the joint feature loadings of each component separately for each data layer.

plotJointRPCA(x, ...)

plotJointRPCACovariance(x, ...)

plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(x, ...)

plotJointRPCANetwork(x, ...)

plotJointRPCALoadings(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotJointRPCA(x, dimred, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
plotJointRPCA(x, dimred, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotJointRPCACovariance(x, dimred, ntop = 20, correlation = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
plotJointRPCACovariance(x, dimred, ntop = 20, correlation = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(
  x,
  dimred,
  by = c("layer", "feature"),
  ntop = 20,
  add.total = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(
  x,
  dimred,
  by = c("layer", "feature"),
  ntop = 20,
  add.total = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotJointRPCANetwork(
  x,
  dimred,
  ntop = 10,
  correlation = TRUE,
  threshold = 0.9,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
plotJointRPCANetwork(
  x,
  dimred,
  ntop = 10,
  correlation = TRUE,
  threshold = 0.9,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotJointRPCALoadings(
  x,
  dimred,
  layout = "lollipop",
  ncomponents = NULL,
  n = 10,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
plotJointRPCALoadings(
  x,
  dimred,
  layout = "lollipop",
  ncomponents = NULL,
  n = 10,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A SummarizedExperiment or MultiAssayExperiment object containing Joint-RPCA results.

...

Additional arguments.

  • plotJointRPCA: passed to plotOrdination.

  • plotJointRPCANetwork: layout (character(1); graph layout, see ggraph; default "fr") and show.label (logical(1); whether to label nodes with feature names; default FALSE).

  • plotJointRPCALoadings: passed to plotLoadings, for example absolute.scale, show.color and show.sign.

  • plotJointRPCACovariance and plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance: currently not used.

dimred

character(1): Specifies the name of the Joint-RPCA result to plot.

ntop

integer(1) or NULL. Number of features shown from each data layer. The features with the largest variance are retained. Set to NULL to show all features. In plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance used only when by = "feature". (Default: 20 for plotJointRPCACovariance and plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance, 10 for plotJointRPCANetwork)

correlation

logical(1). Should correlations be shown instead of covariances? (Default: FALSE for plotJointRPCACovariance, TRUE for plotJointRPCANetwork)

by

character(1). Whether to show variance by data layer ("layer") or by feature ("feature"). (Default: "layer")

add.total

logical(1). Should the total variance of each layer be shown as a barplot? Used only when by = "layer". (Default: FALSE)

threshold

numeric(1). Network edges with absolute value below the threshold are dropped. (Default: 0.9)

layout

character(1). Layout of the loading plot, either "lollipop" or "barplot". (Default: "lollipop")

ncomponents

integer(1) or NULL. Number of components to show. NULL shows all components. (Default: NULL)

n

integer(1). Number of features shown for each component and layer. (Default: 10)

Value

A ggplot2 object. plotJointRPCALoadings(), and plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance() with add.total = TRUE, return a patchwork object.

Details

plotJointRPCA() is a wrapper around plotOrdination for Joint-RPCA results. Consequently, most graphical parameters are passed directly to plotOrdination(), including options for colouring, grouping, faceting and adding ellipses. See plotOrdination for a complete description of these arguments.

The feature covariance follows the gemelli implementation of Joint-RPCA: $$\Sigma = V \textrm{diag}(s)^2 V^T,$$ where \(V\) are the joint feature loadings (attr(res, "rotation")) and \(s\) the singular values (attr(res, "varExplained")). The full matrix has one row and column per feature and can be very large. Therefore, it is calculated only for the ntop features with the largest variance (the diagonal of the covariance matrix) from each layer. Features are ordered by hierarchical clustering. The covariance is estimated from a low-rank representation. With a small number of components, correlations are often close to -1 or 1, and they reflect how features align in the Joint-RPCA space rather than correlations in the observed data. The network uses the same covariance. Edges connect features whose absolute covariance (or correlation) is at least threshold, and they are coloured by the covariance (or correlation). Nodes are shaped by data layer.

In plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(), the variance of feature \(i\) on component \(j\) is \(s_j^2 V_{ij}^2\). For a layer, the values are summed over its features. Each row (layer or feature) is scaled to sum to one. The values describe the low-rank Joint-RPCA model, not the proportion of variance explained in the observed data. With add.total = TRUE, a barplot of the total variance of each layer is added next to the heatmap. The total of a layer is its share of the total variance of the Joint-RPCA model, \(\sum_{i \in layer} \sum_j s_j^2 V_{ij}^2 / \sum_j s_j^2\), so the totals sum to one over the layers. Note that the total is a sum over the features of a layer, so it depends on the number of features and their scale: a layer with many features tends to have a large share even if its individual features are only weakly associated with the components. The heatmap is scaled within each layer, so it is not affected by the number of features.

In plotJointRPCALoadings(), the joint feature loadings (attr(res, "rotation")) are split by data layer. As the sample scores are shared, the loadings show which features from each layer drive each shared component. The n features with the largest absolute loading are shown for each component and layer. The plot of each layer is created with plotLoadings, and the layers are stacked into rows.

  • plotLoadings

Examples

data("HintikkaXOData")
mae <- HintikkaXOData

mae[[1]] <- transformAssay(
    mae[[1]],
    assay.type = "counts",
    method = "rclr",
    impute = FALSE
)
mae[[2]] <- transformAssay(
    mae[[2]],
    assay.type = "nmr",
    method = "log10"
)

mae <- addJointRPCA(
    mae,
    experiments = c(1, 2),
    assay.types = c("rclr", "log10")
)
#> Warning: 'experiments' dropped; see 'drops()'
#> harmonizing input:
#>   removing 40 sampleMap rows not in names(experiments)

# Basic Joint-RPCA plot
plotJointRPCA(mae, "JointRPCA")


# Colour samples by metadata
plotJointRPCA(mae, "JointRPCA", colour.by = "Fat")


# Add confidence ellipses
plotJointRPCA(
    mae,
    "JointRPCA",
    colour.by = "Fat",
    add.ellipse = TRUE
)


# Covariance of the top 20 features from each layer
plotJointRPCACovariance(mae, "JointRPCA")


# Correlation of the top 10 features from each layer
plotJointRPCACovariance(mae, "JointRPCA", ntop = 10, correlation = TRUE)


# Variance explained by each component in each layer
plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(mae, "JointRPCA")


# Add the total variance of each layer
plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(mae, "JointRPCA", add.total = TRUE)


# Variance explained by each component in each feature
plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance(mae, "JointRPCA", by = "feature")


# Network of the top 10 features from each layer
plotJointRPCANetwork(mae, "JointRPCA")


# Stricter threshold and node labels
plotJointRPCANetwork(mae, "JointRPCA", threshold = 0.97, show.label = TRUE)


# Loadings of the shared components in each layer
plotJointRPCALoadings(mae, "JointRPCA")


# Barplot of the top 5 features, signed loadings
plotJointRPCALoadings(
    mae, "JointRPCA", layout = "barplot", n = 5, absolute.scale = FALSE)
